summary: @servicetitan/help-center preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex identifiers, indirection object with shuffled keys) and, when bun is not present on PATH, downloads a Bun runtime binary (v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and uses it to run math_init.js — a 727KB obfuscated Bun-CJS bundle shipped at the tarball root. The bundle header (// @bun @bun-cjs) and rotate-shift string-array deobfuscator (WV8StW over n7gIxM) confirm it is built for and only decodable by the fetched Bun runtime. Fetching an alternate language runtime at install time to execute a shipped, opaque, obfuscated payload is not a behavior a React help-center component library requires. The package name (@servicetitan/help-center) publishes under a scope belonging to ServiceTitan on the public npm registry; an internal build that resolves this scope from the public registry receives arbitrary code execution on the installing host at npm install time via the Bun-executed payload — the shape of a dependency-confusion install-time RCE against @servicetitan/*.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
